messages:
Alex: Heads-up — I'm trying to onboard Kestrel-9B from OpenBench for eval. License scanner just flagged two red things: a redistribution clause that looks like it prohibits distributing derivative weights, and an attribution requirement that seems to demand visible credit in any deployed UI. Can legal weigh in?

Maria: running quant experiments now (q4_0, q5_0). Early numbers: q4 reduces mem by ~2.8x but generation F1 on our eval set drops ~4 pts. Might be ok for lower-cost infra but could be a quality regression for product flows.

Sam: curious if the redistribution clause means we can still host model behind our hosted API if weights are modified by quantization or pruning. Is that considered "distribution"?

LicenseBot: License scan result: https://licensescanner.internal/reports/1749805432 — key excerpt: 
```
Section 3.2: "No redistribution of Derivative Models or modified model weights is permitted without explicit written permission from the licensors."
Section 5.1: "Attribution: All deployments must display the model name and original authors in the user-facing attribution area."
```

Priya (Legal): Thanks for the ping. From that excerpt it sounds like upstream forbids redistributing derivative weights. Hosting behind an API where we don't publish weights is often allowed, but the interpretation hinges on whether our provisioning (e.g., shipping quantized binaries to Dedicated customers or on-prem bundles) counts as redistribution. Quantized weights packaged for a customer => likely redistribution.

Priya (Legal): For attribution: requiring UI attribution is enforceable, but we need to confirm whether the wording requires attribution on any machine-to-machine usage (embeddings used in backend search) or only on customer-facing surfaces. Please send the full license link and the model card.

Alex: posted full license here: https://openbench.org/models/kestrel-9b/license.txt — also attached model card link. Looks like they intentionally blocked derivatives redistribution to prevent third-party forks.

Maria: notes on experiments — cmd I used: 
```
python quantize.py --model kestrel-9b --format q4_0 --calib-samples 1024 --seed 42
```
If we can't redistribute quantized binaries, we could still run quantization in-host (on our infra) and not hand the artifacts to customers. That would allow Dedicated to run the quantization step at deploy-time but we still push the quantized blobs to the GPU hosts we manage. Is that safe?

Priya (Legal): If the quantized blobs are stored/transferred to customer-controlled machines (on-prem, VPC with customer data plane), that is redistribution. For our Hosted API (SaaS) where we control the runtime and never hand weights to customers, that's generally fine, but confirm with upstream. For Dedicated we need to check contract: if dedicated hosts are in our tenancy and we never give the binary to the customer, likely OK. If the Dedicated product hands over an image or files to the customer, that's not OK.

Sam: So practical options: 1) Hosted-only (fastest) 2) Ask upstream for a special redistribution exception for quantized/optimized weights 3) Use runtime-level on-the-fly quantization (never persist deriv weights) 4) Choose a different model.

Lei: what's the UI attribution ask? If it's mandatory visible credit on every chat screen, we need to scope the work for the Console and API docs. Could be friction for PLG.

Priya (Legal): The clause said "display the model name and original authors in the user-facing attribution area." That implies customer-facing UI. For non-UI embeddings usage, it may be enough to include attribution in the API terms or documentation, but I'd rather get clarity. I'll reach out to upstream counsel to ask: (a) can we host quantized/derived weights in our managed runtime, (b) is attribution required for server-side-only uses, (c) can they provide a redistribution carve-out for enterprise customers under NDA/contract.

Alex: Actionable plan:
- Priya to contact upstream and request written clarification + possible carve-out.
- Maria to continue q4_0/q5_0 runs but gate any artifact uploads. Use eval harness to measure quality/regression.
- Sam to document deployment constraints for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
- Lei to draft potential UI attribution placements and small mock for legal review.

Maria: I'll post perf tables once I finish the 10 eval runs (should be by EOD). If quantized perf is acceptable, we can recommend runtime-only quantization as interim.

Priya (Legal): I'll have an initial reply to upstream by EOD; will update here. Meanwhile, do not publish or distribute any modified weight blobs externally.

Alex: thanks all — keeping this thread as the single source. If Priya gets a permissive answer we can proceed to onboard; if not, we pivot to hosted-only or different model. :thumbsup:
